    Primitive category-algebra deletion #

    For the canonical projector at an object of a finite linear category, the primitive ideal annihilates a represented module exactly when the original category module vanishes at that object. This is the objectwise bridge between algebraic primitive deletion and the literal object-deletion quotient.

    Under the projective-generator equivalence, annihilation by the primitive ideal of the projector at X is exactly vanishing at X.

    For a singleton deletion, the primitive-ideal annihilation property is the literal vanishing-on-deleted-objects property.

    The finite modules over the literal object-deletion category are equivalent to the ambient algebra modules annihilated by the corresponding canonical primitive ideal.
